records.text: Owens said odd flights had come from El Paso on the day of Charlie Kirk's assassination
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Remember El Paso, Texas is where all those weird flights were coming from on the day of Charlie Kirk's assassination.

verification.notes: Verification attempted after reviewing the transcript. The statement supplies no tail number, Mode-S/ICAO hex, flight number, route, or time for the alleged El Paso flights. Searches of current and archived public flight records did not yield raw ADS-B evidence that could be cross-checked. Absence from available trackers is not evidence the flights did not occur, so the result is unverifiable rather than false.

records.text: On September 9, a U.S. Air Force plane left Fort Huachuca at 11:43 a.m. local time and flew to El Paso, Texas.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: there was an Air Force plane that became very relevant. I will remind you on September 9th, it left Fort Huachuca at 1143 a.m. local time. ... And it flew to El Paso, Texas.

verification.notes: The surviving AirNav record confirms SAM702 and tail 99-0404 in southern Arizona on September 9, 2025, first seen near Tucson and landing at Eloy. It does not establish an 11:43 Fort Huachuca departure or a flight to El Paso.

records.text: The plane landed in El Paso at 1:31 p.m. local time after a 50-minute hop from Fort Huachuca.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: on September 9th, it left Fort Huachuca at 1143 a.m. local time. ... And it flew to El Paso, Texas. ... This plane could have been somebody that was at the meeting and then went to Texas, landed at 1.31 p.m. local time. It was just a 50-minute hop from El Paso, Texas to Fort Huachuca.

verification.notes: No neutral public flight record located establishes the claimed El Paso landing time or 50-minute Fort Huachuca leg. The transcript also reverses the route in one sentence, increasing uncertainty.

records.text: The plane then flew from El Paso to Andrews Air Force Base using the Special Air Mission call sign SAM 702.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Then that plane flies from El Paso to Andrews Air Force Base in Washington, D.C. The reason that flight was relevant and caught a lot of attention early on was because it used a SAM call sign, SAM 702.

verification.notes: AirNav independently confirms that USAF tail 99-0404 operated as SAM702 in southern Arizona on September 9, 2025. The available record does not establish the claimed El Paso-to-Andrews leg.

sources.title: AirNav Radar flight SAM702
sources.relevance: Confirms SAM702, USAF tail 99-0404, in southern Arizona on September 9, while not confirming the full claimed route.

records.text: Bradley D. Hansell was one of the VIPs aboard SAM 702 when it left Fort Huachuca for El Paso on the morning of September 9, apparently traveling with four other people.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: SAM 702 was leaving Fort Huachuca and heading for El Paso, Texas, in a time frame that would work with this alleged meeting on the morning of September 9th. ... And now we can reveal the name of one of those VIPs who was aboard the plane, apparently with four other people. ... His name is Bradley Hansell.

verification.notes: Bradley Hansell’s official biography confirms his identity and role, but no authoritative passenger manifest or flight log located establishes that he and four other people were aboard SAM702 on the claimed trip. Audited private-travel-record limitation; verification was attempted.

records.text: Candace Owens said the plane flew from Fort Huachuca to El Paso on September 9, arrived at 1:20 p.m. local time, remained for four hours and ten minutes, and returned to Joint Base Andrews.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: then flies from Fort Huachuca to El Paso and arrives at 1 20 p.m local remains on the ground for four hours and 10 minutes and then it returns back to Joint Base Andrews just outside of DC

verification.notes: Current searches found no authoritative aircraft log or official itinerary confirming the claimed September 9 Fort Huachuca-El Paso-Joint Base Andrews route, 1:20 p.m. arrival, or four-hour-ten-minute ground time. The episode’s assertion alone is insufficient.

records.text: Candace Owens said Bradley Hansell's Fort Huachuca stop lasted 19 hours, the longest stop of the trip, and included an overnight stay and a roughly 20-minute helicopter tour of the border.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Makes Fort Huachuca stand out as the center of a trip, for one, because Bradley Hansell remained on the ground the longest there. For 19 hours, that's the longest stop in his trip, he opted to stay overnight at Fort Huachuca before departing the next day for El Paso. He did a quick little 20-minute helicopter tour of the border on that morning as well.

verification.notes: No official itinerary, travel voucher, aircraft record, or public schedule located in current research establishes a 19-hour Fort Huachuca stop, an overnight stay, or a roughly 20-minute border helicopter tour by Hansell. The component facts remain unsupported outside the episode.

records.text: Owens said SAM 702 flew to Tucson on September 8, two days before Charlie Kirk's assassination, remained there about four hours, stayed overnight at Fort Huachuca, and departed for El Paso the next morning.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: The plane that flew to Tucson, Arizona on September 8th, two days before Charlie (Charlie Kirk)'s assassination, landed and hung out in Tucson for about four hours before it carried on to the intel base in Fort Huachuca, Arizona, where it stayed overnight. ... Now, before departing for El Paso, Texas, the next morning—mid-morning on the 9th—it leaves for Texas.

verification.notes: Searches for the SAM 702 identifier and the claimed Tucson, Fort Huachuca, and El Paso itinerary produced no authoritative flight record or official confirmation. Public repetitions trace back to the same podcast investigation.

records.text: A military-contracted aircraft identified as N1098L departed Biggs Army Airfield in El Paso on September 10, 2025; Owens gave the departure time as 6:13 a.m.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: It was contracted by our military for whatever reason. This plane departed from the Biggs Army Airfield at 6:13 a.m. That's down in El Paso, Texas, right?

verification.notes: The aircraft and route are supported: FlightAware’s historical record identifies N1098L flying from Biggs AAF (KBIF) to Kalispell (KGPI) on September 10, 2025, and Leidos describes its contractor-operated Global 6500 Army ISR service. The exact time in the legacy claim is not supported: the historical leg is 1348Z, equivalent to 7:48 a.m. MDT, and a preserved FlightAware screenshot also reports 7:48 a.m., not 6:13 a.m. Thus the departure location/date is supported but the stated departure time is contradicted.
